whatItDoes: Authorize up to $75 million in school-facility bonds. Repair, upgrade and equip classrooms, science laboratories, instructional technology and school facilities; fix roofs, plumbing and electrical systems; and remove asbestos and lead pipes. Property taxes would repay principal and interest. The district estimates $5 million annually, an average and highest rate of $40 per $100,000 of assessed property value, collection through fiscal year 2061–62, and $157 million in total repayment. Tax-rate, repayment and timing estimates may vary and are not binding caps. Bond interest rates must remain within legal limits. yesMeans: Authorize the district to issue up to $75 million in bonds for the listed facilities and levy property taxes to repay them under these conditions.
noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds or their repayment property tax through this measure.

whatItDoes: Combine and renew San Marino Unified’s two existing school parcel taxes at their current combined rate of $1,499 per taxable parcel each year for six years, July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2033. From July 1, 2028, the annual adjustment would equal the lesser of 3% or the specified consumer-price-index change; the board could choose a lower adjustment. Estimated annual revenue is $6.1 million, restricted to the listed educational programs, teachers, counselors, class sizes, libraries and technology. Money must go into a separate fund, with annual collection and spending reports. Existing and new senior/disability exemptions and parcel-combination rules are described below. The measure would replace the $415 Measure R tax from July 2027; the $1,084 Measure E tax is already scheduled to expire that June. Approval requires two-thirds of votes.
yesMeans: Approve the combined six-year parcel tax and its annual adjustment, restricted uses and exemption rules.
noMeans: Do not approve the combined renewal. Measure E would expire June 30, 2027, while the existing $415 Measure R tax would continue through June 30, 2031.

parts.label: Senior and disability exemptions
parts.what: Owner-occupants may apply under district procedures if age 65 or older before June 30 of the preceding fiscal year, receiving Supplemental Security Income for disability at any age, or receiving Social Security Disability Insurance with annual income no greater than 250% of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines. Prior exemptions would continue without a new application, subject to verification of ongoing eligibility.

parts.label: What counts as a parcel
parts.what: A separately billed parcel wholly or partly in the district is taxable. Property exempt from regular property taxes remains exempt. Contiguous parcels with identical ownership used solely as an owner-occupied single-family home may be treated as one parcel under district procedures. If that definition is legally invalid, the fallback is each assessor-numbered parcel in the district, which could increase the number taxed.

parts.label: Inflation, reports and other funding
parts.what: The adjustment uses the Los Angeles metropolitan consumer-price index for the prior 12 months as of December 1; CPI-U is the fallback if that index is unavailable. The board could lower the adjustment when sufficient or appropriate, including in response to state-budget changes. The district’s spending limit would adjust by tax collections. Annual reports are due by December 31. The board could reduce the tax if needed to restore government funding affected by the local tax or improve the district’s fiscal position.

whatItDoes: Renew Las Virgenes Unified’s existing $98-per-parcel annual school tax, without a rate increase, for 12 years beginning July 1, 2028, after the current authorization expires. Estimated annual revenue is $2 million, restricted to core academic, arts, reading, technology and athletics programs, class sizes, teachers, counselors, career advisors and instructional materials. It could not pay administrator salaries, benefits or pensions. A separate account, annual spending reports and the existing Citizens’ Oversight Committee would be required; the official text also continues annual audits. Senior/disability exemptions and eligible contiguous-parcel treatment would continue, with applications due June 15 for new claims and existing exemptions automatically retained subject to eligibility checks. Approval requires two-thirds of votes.
yesMeans: Extend the existing $98 annual parcel tax for 12 years beginning July 1, 2028 under these spending and exemption rules.
noMeans: Do not renew this tax; its current authorization would expire June 30, 2028.

parts.label: Exemption eligibility
parts.what: An owner of a parcel used solely as an owner-occupied single-family home may apply if age 65 or older on or before June 30 of the preceding fiscal year, receiving Supplemental Security Income for disability, or receiving Social Security Disability Insurance with annual income no greater than 250% of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines. New applications are due June 15. Current exemptions continue automatically, subject to checks that eligibility continues.

parts.label: Parcels and other funding
parts.what: Separately billed parcels wholly or partly within the district are covered; parcels exempt from ordinary property taxes remain exempt. Contiguous parcels with identical ownership used solely as an owner-occupied single-family home may be treated as one parcel on an application by June 15. If collecting the tax reduces or offsets other government revenue, the district may stop collecting it or must reduce it enough to restore that revenue.
